# easbridge patches to go-activesync v1.1.0

Upstream: https://github.com/hstern/go-activesync (MIT, see `LICENSE`). This directory is a trimmed copy of tag `v1.1.0`
(commit identical to the Go module proxy zip). Only `eas/`, `wbxml/`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `go.mod`
and `go.sum` are kept; `cmd/`, `testenv/`, `diagrams/`, `eas/easmock/` and CI files were dropped.
The repository root wires it in with `replace github.com/hstern/go-activesync => ./third_party/go-activesync`.

Every changed or added line is marked `easbridge patch N` in the source. The tests live in
`eas/easbridge_patches_test.go` and `wbxml/easbridge_patches_test.go` (`go test ./eas ./wbxml -run Patch -v`). The upstream
test suite still passes unchanged.
Run everything with `make test-vendored` from the repository root.

Patches 1 to 5 are the ones listed in DESIGN section 12. Patches 6 and 7 are additions found while reading the code
(recorded in `docs/TESTING.md` as deviations). Patches 8 and 9 came from the security review of v0.1.0 (v0.1.2).
Patches 10 and 11 came from the first contact with a real Exchange 2019 (v0.1.5, `docs/TESTING.md`, real-Exchange
finding 1), patches 12 and 13 from the second (v0.1.6, finding 2), patch 14 from the third (v0.1.7, finding 3). Patch 15 is the
same fix as patch 12 for the Contacts, Tasks and Notes sync, made for the read-only contacts of v0.2.0 before any contacts code
ran against a real Exchange. All of them are small and could be offered upstream.

| # | Files | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `eas/provision.go` | Provision treats `Policy/Status = 2` ("no policy defined", MS-ASPROV 3.1.5.2) as success: no acknowledgement round trip, stored policy key cleared, `LastPolicy()` nil. | Upstream issue #21: an account without a policy could never run any command. |
| 2 | `eas/provision.go`, `eas/errors.go` | A `<RemoteWipe>` element in a Provision response makes Provision fail with `eas.ErrRemoteWipe` (checked with `errors.Is`), also when it arrives through the automatic re-provision after HTTP 449. Checked before the Policy element, because a wipe may come without one. | Upstream discarded the element, so a wipe request could not be honoured. |
| 3 | `eas/easbridge_patches.go` | New `ApplyEmailChangesWith(ctx, client, folder, changes, ApplyOptions{HardDelete})`. `HardDelete` sends `DeletesAsMoves=0`; otherwise `1`. | Hard delete is wanted only when expunging inside Deleted Items. The old method always sends `1`. |
| 4 | `eas/sync.go` | `EmailSyncOptions.NoDateFilter` omits `FilterType` (all items). `NoBodyTruncation` omits `BodyPreference/TruncationSize`. A positive `BodyTruncationSize` (e.g. 1 MiB) was already sent as given. Defaults unchanged. | `EASBRIDGE_FILTER=all`, and inline MIME up to `EASBRIDGE_MIME_INLINE_MAX` instead of 32 KiB. |
| 5 | `eas/itemoperations.go` | `FetchEmail` adds `MIMESupport=2` to the Fetch `Options` when the body type is MIME (the default). | Exchange may answer a Type 4 request with nothing when MIMESupport is not sent. Harmless if ignored. |
| 6 | `eas/email.go` | `EmailItem.ReadSet` / `FlagSet` say whether `<Read>` / `<Flag>` were present (an empty `<Flag/>` means "cleared"). | A Sync `<Change>` carries only changed properties. `Read=false` could not be told apart from "not mentioned", so any flag change would have marked the message unread. |
| 7 | `eas/easbridge_patches.go`, `eas/changes.go`, `eas/sync.go` | `ApplyEmailChangesWith` sends `GetChanges=0`, never bootstraps or resets the key itself (status 3 is returned to the caller), and returns any server `Add/Change/Delete` commands in the response as `ApplyResult.ServerChanges`. Internal refactor: `buildChangeCommands` and `parseSyncCommands` extracted, behaviour of the old code unchanged. | Upstream `ApplyEmailChanges` stores the new SyncKey but drops server commands in the same response; the server never resends them, so mail could be lost. |
| 8 | `wbxml/codepages.go`, `eas/provision.go`, `eas/errors.go`, `eas/interfaces.go` | The Provision code page (14) is now the table of MS-ASWBXML 2.1.2.1.15 token for token. Upstream had invented names from `0x0E` on (so `AccountOnlyRemoteWipe`, token `0x3B`, was decoded as `Hash`). Provision reports `<AccountOnlyRemoteWipe>` (EAS 16.1) as `eas.ErrAccountOnlyRemoteWipe`, which also matches `eas.ErrRemoteWipe`, also through the 449 re-provision; a full `RemoteWipe` wins if both come. New `AcknowledgeAccountOnlyRemoteWipe(ctx, status)` sends `Provision/AccountOnlyRemoteWipe/Status` (MS-ASPROV 3.1.5.1.2.3). | An account-only wipe order went unnoticed, and policy documents were read under wrong names (the policy is only cached, never enforced). |
| 9 | `eas/errors.go`, `eas/client.go`, `eas/options.go` | `HTTPError.RetryAfter` carries the raw `Retry-After` header of an error response (empty if none). Nothing else changes. | A throttled server (429, 503) says how long to wait there. The bridge's circuit breaker honours it; without the field the delay was invisible to callers. |
| 10 | `eas/client.go`, `eas/provision.go`, `eas/settings.go`, `eas/easbridge_patches.go` | New `Config.DeviceInformation *DeviceInformation` (nil keeps the upstream behaviour). When it is set and `ASVersion` is 14.1, 16.0 or 16.1, the **initial** Provision request (the policy download, also when the library re-provisions after an HTTP 449 or a status of patch 11) carries `<settings:DeviceInformation><settings:Set>...` as the first child of `Provision`, in front of `Policies`, with the elements `Model`, `IMEI`, `FriendlyName`, `OS`, `OSLanguage`, `PhoneNumber`, `MobileOperator`, `UserAgent`, `EnableOutboundSMS` that the struct holds (empty ones are left out). The acknowledgement never carries it, and no Provision request on 14.0, 12.x or 2.5 does. On the wire: SWITCH_PAGE 14 `Provision` (0x05), SWITCH_PAGE 18 (Settings) `DeviceInformation` (0x16), `Set` (0x08), the children (`Model` 0x17, `FriendlyName` 0x19, `OS` 0x1A, `OSLanguage` 0x1B, `UserAgent` 0x20, `EnableOutboundSMS` 0x21), SWITCH_PAGE 14 `Policies` (0x06). The element is built by `deviceInformationElement`, which `SettingsDeviceInformation` uses too (its output is unchanged); `NewClient` refuses a configuration without `Model` (MS-ASPROV 2.2.2.53: the `Set` must at least hold `Model`); a refused `settings:Status` in the answer is logged, not an error; `DeviceInformationInProvision(version)` tells callers whether a version carries it in Provision. | MS-ASPROV 2.2.2.53: from 14.1 on the client MUST send `settings:DeviceInformation` in the initial Provision request and not on later ones; on 14.0 and 12.x it MUST NOT send it in Provision (a Settings command after provisioning is the way there). Exchange 2019 answers a 14.1+ Provision without it with common status 165 (DeviceInformationRequired, MS-ASCMD 2.2.2). The library only had the separate Settings command, which does not count, and its documentation said it should come before Provision. |
| 11 | `eas/client.go` | `post` answers a response whose top-level `Status` is 140, 142, 143 or 144 (RemoteWipeRequested, DeviceNotProvisioned, PolicyRefresh, InvalidPolicyKey) like an HTTP 449: `Provision()` once, then the command once more. Whatever the second answer is, it is returned. Provision itself is never re-provisioned. A wipe order that arrives in that Provision is surfaced as `ErrRemoteWipe`/`ErrAccountOnlyRemoteWipe` (patches 2 and 8). | MS-ASCMD 2.2.2: for protocol 14.0 and later these statuses, not an HTTP 449, tell the device to provision again ("provision to get the request" for 140). Without this the status surfaced as an error and nothing ever re-provisioned, so a policy refresh could stop a long-running session for good. |
| 12 | `eas/sync.go` | `buildSyncRequest`: the request for a first SyncKey (SyncKey `0`) holds `SyncKey` and `CollectionId` and nothing else. It used to add `DeletesAsMoves=1`, `GetChanges=1`, `WindowSize` and `Options`; the second request, with the key the server issued, still carries all of them. The children of `Options` now follow the order of the specification's examples (`FilterType`, `BodyPreference`, `BodyPartPreference`, `MIMESupport`, `MIMETruncation`, `RightsManagementSupport`). | MS-ASCMD 2.2.3.84: a Sync with SyncKey 0 and `GetChanges` set to 1 or empty is answered Status 4 (protocol error); Exchange 2019 did exactly that to the bridge's first Sync. MS-ASCMD 3.1.5.4 describes the initial request as the SyncKey and the CollectionId; the options are sticky and are sent again with every later request. The order in `Options` is free (AirSync.xsd makes it an unbounded choice), the examples of 4.5.7 put `BodyPreference` before `MIMESupport`. |
| 13 | `wbxml/codepages.go`, `wbxml/decode.go`, `eas/client.go` | The AirSyncBase table gains its 16.0 and 16.1 tags (0x1C to 0x2D: `Add`, `Delete`, `ClientId`, `Content`, `Location` and its parts, `InstanceId`) and ComposeMail 0x15 to 0x18. New `Registry.TolerateUnknownTags()`: `Unmarshal` names a tag it does not know `Unknown_<page>_0x<token>` (content and children kept) instead of failing the whole message; the default registry of `eas.NewClient` uses it. `Marshal` stays strict; `wbxml.DefaultRegistry()` alone still refuses unknown tags (upstream test). | The tables were transcribed for 14.1. A meeting request in a 16.x Sync carries `airsyncbase:Location` (MS-ASWBXML 2.1.2.1.3, note 3 under Code Page 2), which no table knew, and one unknown token failed the decoding of the whole Sync response, so a folder with a meeting invitation in its window could never be synced. Every page the bridge decodes was compared with MS-ASWBXML token for token (`TestPatch13_codePagesMatchTheSpecificationTokenForToken`). |
| 14 | `eas/email.go` | `parseBody` reads the content of `airsyncbase:Data` as every chunk in document order, inline strings (STR_I) and OPAQUE alike (new `bodyData`), and decides afterwards: a body of Type 4 (MIME) goes to `BodyMIME`, in whatever form it came and whatever the order of `Type` and `Data`; any OPAQUE chunk is still taken for MIME as before; every other type keeps its text in `Body`. `BodyMIME` is a copy that shares nothing with the decoded tree and stays `nil` for an empty `Data`. | Real-Exchange finding 3: Exchange 2019 sends the MIME of a Type 4 body, in an ItemOperations Fetch and in a Sync, as an inline string, not as OPAQUE. Upstream took only the first OPAQUE chunk as MIME and read an inline string as text for `Body`, so `BodyMIME` stayed empty: `Fetch: upstream: item has no MIME body` although the message was there, and no Sync could hand over a message inline. The other places in the library that read `Data` (documents, attachments, certificates, pictures, calendar bodies) already take both forms. |
| 15 | `eas/contacts.go` | `genericSyncFolder` (the Sync of Contacts, Tasks and Notes): the request for a first SyncKey (SyncKey `0`) holds `SyncKey` and `CollectionId` and nothing else. It used to add `DeletesAsMoves=1`, `GetChanges=1` and `WindowSize=100`; the request with the key the server issued still carries all three. | The same rule as patch 12: MS-ASCMD 2.2.3.84 makes the server answer status 4 (protocol error) to `GetChanges` set to 1 or empty with SyncKey 0, and 3.1.5.4 describes the initial request as the key and the collection. Real Exchange refused the mail Sync for exactly this in v0.1.5; the contacts sync of v0.2.0 would have met the same refusal. The wire-level model of `internal/easupstream` now refuses it for any collection. |

## Not patched (handled in `internal/easupstream`)

- Status names: `eas/status.go` names 141 to 145 and 177 one code off (it calls 144 ExternallyManagedDevicesNotAllowed and
  177 ItemNotFoundInCollection; MS-ASCMD 2.2.2 says 141 LegacyDeviceOnStrictPolicy, 142 DeviceNotProvisioned, 143
  PolicyRefresh, 144 InvalidPolicyKey, 145 ExternallyManagedDevicesNotAllowed, 177 MaximumDevicesReached), and an upstream
  test asserts the wrong names, so the table is left alone to keep the upstream tests unchanged. The bridge never shows the
  library's name for those codes: `internal/easupstream/statuses.go` has its own table from the specification, and a test
  checks that every code the library mislabels is in it.
- `buildSyncRequest` writes `Wait` and `HeartbeatInterval` in front of `Collections`; MS-ASCMD 6.45 (Sync Request Schema) puts
  them after it (Collections, Wait, HeartbeatInterval, WindowSize, Partial). The bridge uses Ping, never a long Sync, so the
  option is not used and was left alone.
- FolderSync status 9: the adapter resets the hierarchy key and retries once.
- Sync status 12 / 14, Ping statuses (the library returns the result together with an error), protocol version choice
  (`NegotiateVersion` is never called), `NoBootstrap` for every Sync, `http://` rejection, logger wrapping that drops the
  `User` query value, HTTP timeouts, and persistence of keys (staged, committed by the engine).

## Updating

Re-vendor from the module cache, re-apply by `git diff` against the first commit of this directory, and run
`make test-vendored`. Do not drop a patch without removing its test.
